title: Add FDM enclosure solver dependency
description: Adds the tscircuitcreate-fdm-enclosure dependency to the aggregate package, allowing the package updater to complete its dependency synchronization without failure.
body:
## Summary

- add `@tscircuit/create-fdm-enclosure@0.0.2` to the aggregate package dependencies
- replay the package versions from the updater run that was blocked by the missing dependency
- update `bun.lock` with the enclosure solver and its transitive dependencies

## Root cause

After `@tscircuit/core` added the enclosure solver as a peer dependency, `scripts/copy-core-versions.ts` detected that the aggregate `tscircuit` package did not declare it and threw:

```
Missing core dependencies in package.json: @tscircuit/create-fdm-enclosure
```

This caused the two latest **Update @tscircuit Package** workflow runs to fail before they could create their dependency-update PR.

## Impact

The aggregate package now supplies core's enclosure solver peer dependency. The package updater can complete its dependency synchronization instead of failing during `copy-core-versions`.

## Validation

- reproduced the exact failed workflow step:
  - `bun update --latest @tscircuit/core @tscircuit/cli @tscircuit/eval @tscircuit/runframe`
  - `bun run copy-core-versions`
- `bun install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts`
- `bun run build`
- `bun test` — 3 passing

title: Add pill pads to DFN footprints
description: Adds support for stadium-shaped copper pads in DFN footprints by modifying the DFN generator to honor the inherited pillpads parameter and exposing it in the typed DFN builder.
body:
## What changed

- make the DFN generator honor the inherited `pillpads` parameter
- expose `.pillpads(...)` on the typed DFN builder
- verify pad shape and radius with an SVG visual snapshot

## Why

Several imported JLCPCB DFN packages use stadium-shaped copper pads. The DFN schema already accepted `pillpads`, but the generator always emitted rectangular pads and the typed builder did not expose the option.

This is the footprinter prerequisite for exact matches such as BME280, U3018, PC400J00000F, SN74LVC1G123DCTR, and TC7WH157FU. A follow-up `circuit-json-to-footprinter` change is still needed to prioritize shape-matching seeds within its optimization cap; the standalone 250-board benchmark therefore remains 133/250 with the current matcher.

## Validation

- `bun test` — 451 passing
- `bun run build`
- `bunx biome format src/fn/dfn.ts src/footprinter.ts tests/dfn.test.ts`
- visually inspected `dfn8_pillpads.snap.svg`
- sequential 250-board jlc5000 benchmark — 133/250, zero errors with the current matcher

title: Add pill pads to quad footprints
description: Adds a _pillpads option to the quad generator, allowing for pill-shaped perimeter pads while maintaining rectangular thermal pads, improving the representation of imported EasyEDAJLC quad footprints.
body:
## What

- add a `_pillpads` option to the shared quad generator and expose it through QFN, QFP, TQFP, LQFP, MLP, and quad builders
- emit pill-shaped perimeter pads while keeping QFN thermal pads rectangular
- calculate pill radius from the shorter pad dimension so vertical and horizontal pads are both valid

## Why

Imported EasyEDA/JLC quad footprints frequently use pill-shaped copper pads. The quad generator could only emit rectangles, so `circuit-json-to-footprinter` could optimize the dimensions but could not represent the source geometry closely enough to cross the 98% IoU benchmark threshold.

## Impact

Tested with tscircuit/circuit-json-to-footprinter#16 against the 250-board tscircuit/jlc5000 corpus:

- published footprinter control: 91/250 at or above 98% IoU (36.4%)
- this branch: 99/250 (39.6%)
- eight additional boards cross the threshold, all selecting `qfn..._pillpads` strings
- combined with the matcher PR, the currently published 85/250 baseline rises to 99/250

## Checks

- `bun test` (450 pass, 0 fail)
- `bun run build`
- `bunx biome check src/fn/quad.ts src/helpers/pillpad.ts src/footprinter.ts tests/qfn.test.ts`
- `git diff --check`

title: Prefer readable pin names for anonymous schematic nets
description: Replaces generated slash-joined schematic net labels with readable component-pin labels, improving schematic readability and maintaining explicit trace labels.
body:
## Summary

- replace generated slash-joined schematic net labels such as `A/B/C` with one readable component-pin label
- choose a pin from the connected component with the highest pin count, using the lower component name and lower pin number as deterministic tie-breakers
- apply the fallback consistently to explicit traces, component `connections`, and source-port fallbacks
- preserve explicit trace labels and named nets such as `GND` and `VCC`
- refresh affected schematic and simulation snapshots

## Why

Slash-joined anonymous labels can become extremely long and make larger schematics difficult to read. A stable label such as `U1_X1` keeps the schematic compact while still identifying the net by a useful endpoint.

## Validation

- focused explicit-label, named-net, lower-pin, and `connections` regressions pass
- formatting and diff checks pass

title: Update enclosure snapshots for opaque PoppyGL rendering
description: Updates the enclosure snapshots to use PoppyGL 0.0.26, ensuring that the rendered images display fully opaque pixels instead of translucent ones.
body:
## Summary

- require `poppygl@^0.0.26` for 3D snapshot tests
- regenerate the angled and top-down FDM enclosure snapshots with the merged glTF alpha-mode fix
- replace the half-transparent enclosure pixels with fully opaque output

## Root cause

The enclosure snapshots were generated with PoppyGL 0.0.25. That renderer wrote `baseColorFactor[3]` into the PNG even when the glTF material used `alphaMode: "OPAQUE"`, leaving the enclosure pixels at alpha 127/255. PoppyGL 0.0.26 honors the alpha mode and writes opaque pixels.

## Impact

The enclosure snapshots no longer display a checkerboard/translucent wall region in GitHub's PNG viewer. Both updated PNGs have an alpha range of 255–255.

[tscircuit/tscircuit#4036](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit/pull/4036) should merge first so this core release's downstream package update is not blocked by the newly required enclosure solver.

## Validation

- `bun test tests/enclosure/enclosure-fdm-box-usb-cutout.test.tsx`
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run build`
- ImageMagick alpha inspection reports `opaque=True`, `alpha-min=1`, and `alpha-max=1` for both snapshots

title: Generate namespaced FDM enclosures
description: Adds namespaced TSX elements for FDM enclosures, including the construction of a solver for generating enclosures based on PCB components and their apertures, along with 3D rendering capabilities.
body:
## Summary

- adds `<enclosure.fdm.Box boardRef="..." />` and `<enclosure.cutoutaperture />` namespaced TSX elements
- constructs `CreateFdmEnclosureSolver` from the referenced board and component-owned apertures
- registers the solver in core and emits `solver:started` with reconstructable constructor input for the standard solver debugger
- emits an opaque JSCAD-backed `cad_component` positioned below the board
- adds angled and top-down orthographic 3D snapshots using a ModelCDN USB-C connector

## Placement behavior

Each aperture owns the conversion from its nearest PCB component into the solver input. Its nearest enclosure wall and offset come from the component's cable insertion center when available. The aperture center is placed above the PCB using the floor thickness, board thickness, aperture dimensions, and margin.

## Package

Uses `@tscircuit/create-fdm-enclosure@0.0.2`, published through that repository's standard `bun-pver-release.yml` workflow.

description: Moves the SchematicBox primitive into its own directory and updates its public export, derives local ID aliases from canonical Circuit JSON interfaces, renames mappings for clarity, and prepares layout trees for multiple schematic representations without changing existing runtime behavior.

## Summary

- Move the `SchematicBox` primitive into its own `/SchematicBox` directory and update its public export.
- Derive local `SourceComponentId`, `SourceGroupId`, and `SchematicSheetId` aliases from canonical Circuit JSON interfaces where the mappings are defined.

- Return layout trees with their typed schematic sheet ID and pass it through `applySchematicMatchPackLayoutToTree`.

## Why

This is a behavior-neutral prerequisite for the multi-sheet chip representation work. Landing the organization, naming, typing, and layout API plumbing separately keeps the follow-up feature PR focused on creating and routing the additional chip representations.

## Impact

No runtime behavior changes are intended for existing circuits. A source component currently has one schematic representation per layout tree, while the new optional sheet context prepares MatchPack for multiple representations.

## Summary

- classify in-stock TFT support ICs as display controllers, bias/power ICs, gamma buffers, or backlight drivers
- add package, driver type, basic-part, and preferred-part filters

## Data selection

JLCPCB's catalog does not expose a dedicated TFT-driver subcategory. The route therefore starts with the existing `LCD Drivers` and `LED Drivers` catalog groups, then selects curated TFT-oriented manufacturer family prefixes. The current production catalog includes matching parts such as SSD1963 controllers, TPS651/AW375 bias ICs, BUF168 gamma buffers, and AP3041/AP5727 backlight drivers.

No derived-table rebuild is required; the page reads directly from `component_catalog`.

title: Fix LCD display list and add LCD driver page
description: Fixes the LCD display derived table population and adds a new page for listing LCD drivers with filtering options.
body:
## Summary

- populate the LCD display derived table from current and historical LCD display subcategories
- add a separate `/lcd_drivers/list` page backed by the existing component catalog
- support package, Basic, and Preferred filters on the LCD driver page
- show LCD driver pricing, stock, and catalog attributes
- add regression coverage for candidate selection, driver queries, filters, and rendering

## Root cause

The LCD display derived-table builder selected candidates with a `description LIKE "%LCD%"` predicate. Synced catalog descriptions are now blank, so rebuilds produced an empty `lcd_display` table even though LCD modules remain available under dedicated subcategories.

LCD driver ICs are intentionally kept separate from display modules. The new driver route selects the existing `LCD Drivers` catalog subcategory directly, avoiding a second derived table and excluding unrelated display hardware.

## Impact

- after rebuilding and syncing `lcd_display`, `/lcd_display/list` and its JSON endpoint will return LCD modules again
- after deploying the worker, `/lcd_drivers/list` and `/lcd_drivers/list.json` will list in-stock LCD driver chips without an additional database rebuild

title: Improve TSX transform recovery and errors
description: Fixes TSX transform errors by allowing block comments between component props and providing clearer error messages for syntax issues.
body:
## What changed

- Retry TSX transforms by converting a single JSX-style block comment between component props into the equivalent valid block-comment syntax.
- Only accept a repair when that isolated change makes the entire file parse, preserving valid JSX child comments and comment-like string contents.
- Separate transform failures from runtime evaluation failures.
- Format remaining syntax errors with the source filename, line/column, surrounding source, and a caret.
- Rename the opaque `Eval compiled js error` runtime wrapper to `Error evaluating "<file>"`.

## Root cause

The reported circuit placed `{/* ... */}` between `<chip` props. That form is valid for JSX children but invalid inside an opening tag. Sucrase reported it as an unexpected token, and `importLocalFile` then caught the transform exception together with runtime exceptions and mislabeled it as a compiled-JS evaluation failure.

## User impact

The reported generated TSX now evaluates without requiring the user to rewrite unrelated constructs such as the anonymous default export, `Array.from` arrow callback, em-dash, or `$` identifier. Other syntax failures now point directly at source instead of presenting an opaque nested transform/eval message.

## Validation

- `bun test tests/repros/jsx-comment-between-props.test.tsx tests/examples/example09-not-defined-component.test.tsx`
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run format:check`
- `bun run build`
- Full suite exercised 147 passing tests before worker tests hit the checkout's initially missing build artifacts; after building, all affected worker/error tests passed on focused rerun.

title: Fix physical net in hypergraph pathing
description: Fixes routing failures caused by incorrect physical net IDs in hypergraph construction, ensuring consistent net identity during autorouting.

It’s basically two PRs:

* Merge this PR into the current branch: https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/1733
* Put the rest of the changes in this PR.


## Summary

- require connMap-backed canonical physical-net IDs when building hypergraphs
- carry canonical IDs through tiny-hypergraph/BFS routing and fail loudly when they are missing

- add SRJ23 sample 003 and focused buildHyperGraph regression coverage
- refresh only routing snapshots changed by the corrected net identity

## Root cause

Aliases belonging to the same physical net could receive different routing identities because hypergraph construction used connection/root names instead of the connectivity map. Selective reripping then treated same-net copper as a blocker and repeatedly failed to route SRJ23 sample 003.

title: Preserve SRJ root connection identities in hypergraph pathing
description: Preserves SRJ root connection identities for accurate trace-width and connectivity lookups in hypergraph pathing.
body:
## Summary

- derive `PortPoint.rootConnectionName` only from `simpleRouteConnection.__rootConnectionNames`
- keep `mutuallyConnectedNetworkId` limited to canonical physical-net grouping and BFS blocking
- preserve SRJ root identity across tiny-hypergraph serialization using the original connection metadata

## Root cause

The canonical connectivity-map net ID was reused as `rootConnectionName`. Downstream solvers interpret `rootConnectionName` as an original SRJ/configuration identity, so trace-width lookup could receive a generated connectivity ID instead of the SRJ connection name.

## Impact

Routes retain their original SRJ root identity for downstream trace-width and connectivity lookups while canonical physical-net behavior remains unchanged.

title: Fix alpha handling for opaque glTF materials
description: Fixes rendering of opaque glTF materials by ensuring OPAQUE fragments write a fully opaque alpha value, while MASK fragments become opaque after passing the cutoff, and BLEND materials retain their fractional alpha behavior.
body:
## Summary

- force glTF `OPAQUE` fragments to write a fully opaque alpha value
- make `MASK` fragments fully opaque after they pass the cutoff
- preserve the existing fractional-alpha behavior for `BLEND` materials
- add focused value-level regression coverage for all three alpha modes
- add a visual PNG snapshot showing opaque, masked, and blended materials side by side
- document in `AGENTS.md` that tests need visual snapshots

## Root cause

The software renderer used `baseColorFactor[3]` as the output PNG alpha even when a material's glTF `alphaMode` was `OPAQUE`. This allowed a material such as `baseColorFactor: [0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5]` with `alphaMode: "OPAQUE"` to produce half-transparent PNG pixels. It caused opaque enclosure geometry generated by circuit-json-to-gltf to appear as checkerboard transparency in core snapshots.

## Impact

Opaque enclosure and component geometry now renders with alpha 255, matching glTF alpha-mode semantics. Masked materials remain discarded below the cutoff and are opaque above it; blended materials remain translucent.

## Validation

- `bun test` — 26 passing, including the new visual snapshot
- `bun run format:check`
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run build`
- rendered the core enclosure GLB end to end with a white background; output alpha range is 255–255

title: add DRC-scored via-in-pad topology repairs
description: Add opt-in via-in-pad topology candidates to GlobalDrcForceImproveSolver, allowing GlobalDrcBranchPortfolioSolver to run these candidates as its final internal phase, relocating terminal-side vias and moving fully single-layer terminal routes using pad-centered transitions, while validating that the drilled hole fits inside each connected single-layer terminal pad before proposing a candidate and scoring every valid topology candidate with the caller-provided full DRC evaluator.
body:
## Summary

- add opt-in via-in-pad topology candidates to `GlobalDrcForceImproveSolver`
- let `GlobalDrcBranchPortfolioSolver` run those candidates as its final internal phase
- relocate terminal-side vias and move fully single-layer terminal routes using pad-centered transitions
- accept the board's via drill diameter independently from the outer via land diameter
- validate that the drilled hole fits inside each connected single-layer terminal pad before proposing a candidate
- score every valid topology candidate with the caller-provided full DRC evaluator and reject regressions

## Why

Dense terminal fields can require a layer transition inside the connected terminal pad. Local point-force moves cannot make that topology change, so the repair belongs in the global DRC solver that already compares alternative route candidates.

Via-in-pad eligibility is a solver invariant, not an autorouter-specific mask. The important containment rule is that the drilled hole remains inside the pad copper. A same-net outer via land may extend past the terminal pad, so comparing the full via diameter to the pad dimensions incorrectly rejects valid repairs on small pads.

`viaHoleDiameter` is therefore forwarded through `GlobalDrcForceImproveSolver` to both via-in-pad mutations. When it is omitted, the existing route via diameter remains the conservative fallback for callers that do not distinguish land and drill sizes.

## Dataset 18 verification

With the corresponding autorouter integration pinned to this commit, the full 16-sample Blacksmith benchmark falls from the regressed artifact's 548 total DRCs to 421. The affected samples are:

| Sample | Regressed artifact | Fixed Blacksmith run |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 13 | 105 | 54 |
| 14 | 138 | 93 |
| 16 | 5 | 5 |

The test suite also covers a 0.15 mm drill accepted in a 0.20 mm terminal pad with a 0.30 mm outer via land, while rejecting a 0.10 mm pad.

## Validation

- `bun test --timeout 9999999` — 29 pass, 0 fail
- `bun run typecheck` — pass
- `bun run formatcheck` — pass
- consuming autorouter `bun run build` — pass, including declaration generation
- full Dataset 18 Blacksmith benchmark — 421 total DRCs, all 16 samples completed

title: Prioritize pill-shaped footprint seeds
description: Prioritizes one exact pad-shape seed per footprint family when the target contains pill pads, while keeping ordinary rectangular targets on the existing seed-selection path, and updates the footprinter for DFN pill-pad generation.
body:
## What changed

- prioritize one exact pad-shape seed per footprint family when the target contains pill pads
- keep ordinary rectangular targets on the existing seed-selection path
- update `@tscircuit/footprinter` to 0.0.382 for DFN pill-pad generation
- add a real C92489 BME280 regression
- carry the orientation-aware seed initialization from #22 onto `main` because #22 was merged into the former #20 feature branch rather than the default branch

## Why

The matcher generated `_pillpads` variants, but its ten-seed optimization cap was usually filled by several rotations of rectangular candidates before the shape-compatible DFN seed was optimized. Selecting the strongest pill-compatible candidate from distinct families gives the optimizer access to exact geometry without increasing the optimization budget.

The heuristic is limited to pill-bearing targets. Applying it to normal rectangular pads can promote a lower-IoU package-family candidate through the domain-score bonus.

## Benchmark

Sequential run across all 250 jlc5000 boards:

- current `main`: 97/250 at 98%+ copper IoU (38.8%)
- orientation-only baseline: 133/250 (53.2%)
- this branch: 140/250 (56.0%)
- seven new exact matches over the orientation baseline
- eight raw-IoU improvements and zero regressions
- zero benchmark errors

New exact matches include BME280, SN74LVC2G132DCUR, U3018, AMC1301DWVR, PC400J00000F, SN74LVC1G123DCTR, and TC7WH157FU.

title: Initialize rotated seeds with oriented dimensions

- swap width and height heuristics when optimizing seeds rotated by 90° or 270°
- use those oriented dimensions for active-parameter detection, initialization, step sizing, and bounds

## Why

Target bounds are measured in world axes, while footprinter width and height parameters remain in the seed local axes. Starting a quarter-turned seed with the unswapped dimensions sends the optimizer toward the wrong geometry and can leave otherwise exact matches below the benchmark threshold.

## Benchmark

- before: 97/250 at 98%+ copper IoU (38.8%)
- after: 133/250 at 98%+ copper IoU (53.2%)
- 36 new passing components

title: fix: distinguish EasyEDA HTTP 403 rate limiting from component lookup failure
description: Fixes the error message for EasyEDA API rate limiting to clearly indicate a 403 status instead of a generic lookup failure, providing users with specific guidance on the rate limit and cooldown period.
body:
Fixes #409 — the error-text distinction (suggestion 3 of the issue).

## Problem

EasyEDA's component API rate-limits by IP and answers **HTTP 403** once tripped (not 429, no `Retry-After`). `fetchEasyEDAComponent` treated any non-success response as a lookup failure, so a throttled batch surfaced as:

```
Error: Failed to search for the component
```

which points the user at the part number. The part is fine; the request was throttled — as measured in #409, every LCSC id 403s identically mid-cooldown and recovers after ~2 minutes.

## Change (minimal, one concern)

- A **403** on either the search request or the component-details request now throws a rate-limit-specific error naming the part, stating it's an IP-based limit, and giving the ~2 minute cooldown hint from the issue's measurements.
- Other non-success statuses keep their existing messages but now include the HTTP status code.
- `Component not found` (successful response, empty result list) is **unchanged** — it stays distinct from rate limiting, which is the core complaint in #409.

Retry/backoff, serialising the parts-engine batch, and CDN proxying (suggestions 1, 2, 4) are deliberately left as follow-ups — they're behaviour/architecture decisions, and per review feedback on other PRs I'm keeping one change per PR.

## Tests (red→green)

`tests/fetch-tests/rate-limit-403.test.ts` — uses the existing injectable `fetch` option, so **no network** (unlike the live-API fetch tests, these can't themselves be rate-limited):

1. search-request 403 → `/rate limit/i` error (was: generic lookup failure) — **red before, green after**
2. component-details 403 → `/rate limit/i` error — **red before, green after**
3. empty search result → still exactly `Component not found` (guards the distinction)
4. non-403 failure (500) → message includes `HTTP 500` — **red before, green after**

`bun test` on the new file: 4 pass. `tsc --noEmit` clean. `biome check` clean.

Note: #393 (May) adds part numbers to these messages but doesn't distinguish status codes; this PR is orthogonal and touches only the status-code branches.

title: Infer schematic sheets from schematic box connections
description: Adds support for assigning a board-level schematicbox  to a schematicsheet  with schSheetName, and automatically places components connected to the boxs represented chip pins on the same sheet.
body:
## What changed

This PR adds support for assigning a board-level `<schematicbox />` to a `<schematicsheet />` with `schSheetName`, and automatically places components connected to the box's represented chip pins on the same sheet.

- updates `@tscircuit/props` to `^0.0.589` for `schematicbox.schSheetName`
- adds sheet resolution for sibling `<schematicbox />` elements
- infers a connected component's sheet from source connectivity when exactly one schematic sheet is implied
- preserves explicit or inherited `schSheetName` placement
- leaves components unassigned when their connections imply multiple sheets
- adds stacked schematic and PCB snapshots covering two boxes that represent one physical chip

This follows the prop addition in [tscircuit/props#747](https://github.com/tscircuit/props/pull/747).

## Example

```tsx
<schematicsheet name="Power Sheet" sheetIndex={0} />

<schematicbox
  name="U1 Power"
  schSheetName="Power Sheet"
  chipRef=".U1"
  pinLabels={{ pin1: "VDD", pin2: "GND", pin3: "RESET" }}
  schPinArrangement={{
    leftSide: ["pin1", "pin2", "pin3"],
    rightSide: [],
  }}
/>

<resistor
  name="R1"
  resistance="10k"
  connections={{ pin1: "U1.RESET" }}
/>
```

`R1` does not specify `schSheetName`. Its connection to `U1.RESET`, represented by the `U1 Power` schematic box, places it on `Power Sheet` automatically.

## Implementation

Source connectivity keys are available before schematic rendering. For each schematic box, the implementation maps its represented chip pins to the box's resolved sheet. A normal component receives an inferred sheet only when all matching connections resolve to one unique sheet.

The physical chip referenced by the schematic boxes is excluded from inference so that its regular schematic symbol is not rendered alongside the box representation.

![Two schematic sheets with connected components inferred from schematic-box pins](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/core/da17db77c9646a0300056c46c969189ed7c5a751/tests/features/schematic-sheet/__snapshots__/schematic-sheet05-schematic_stacked.snap.svg)

### PCB

title: fix: defaultTraceWidth/nominalTraceWidth board props now control autorouted trace width
description: Fixes autorouting to respect defaultTraceWidth and nominalTraceWidth properties for trace width control.
body:
Fixes #2620

## What & why

`<board defaultTraceWidth="0.3mm">` (and `nominalTraceWidth`) had no effect on autorouted trace width — every autorouted segment came out at 0.15mm, exactly as diagnosed in the issue:

1. `Group._runLocalAutorouting` only read `props.minTraceWidth` / `props.nominalTraceWidth`; `defaultTraceWidth` was accepted by the props schema but never read anywhere in core.
2. `getSimpleRouteJsonFromCircuitJson` filled each connection's `nominalTraceWidth`/`width` from `minTraceWidth ?? board.min_trace_width ?? 0.1` and only stored its `nominalTraceWidth` parameter as the top-level `SimpleRouteJson.nominalTraceWidth`, which the capacity autorouter's `TraceWidthSolver` ignores (it consumes per-connection `nominalTraceWidth`).

## Changes

- **`Group._runLocalAutorouting`**: the nominal width passed to the SRJ builder is now `props.defaultTraceWidth ?? props.nominalTraceWidth ?? minTraceWidth`.
- **`getSimpleRouteJsonFromCircuitJson`**: connections without an explicit width (e.g. from a `<trace thickness>`) now default to the `nominalTraceWidth` parameter when provided; `minTraceWidth` remains the routing lower bound only (`SimpleRouteJson.minTraceWidth` is still computed from it).
- **Legacy remote solve-endpoint path**: passes the same `defaultTraceWidth ?? nominalTraceWidth` preference (previously passed raw `this.props.nominalTraceWidth` and also dropped `defaultTraceWidth`).
- Behavior is unchanged when neither prop is set (still 0.15mm), and an explicit `<trace thickness>` still takes precedence.

## Tests

- Updated `tests/components/primitive-components/trace-default-trace-width.test.tsx`, which previously asserted the buggy behavior (`width === 0.15` with a "Bug repro" note saying the fixed behavior should be 0.3) — it now asserts 0.3mm, and its PCB snapshot was regenerated (the routed trace is visibly wider).
- Added `tests/features/board-default-trace-width-autorouting.test.tsx` covering: `nominalTraceWidth` on the board, explicit `thickness` precedence over `defaultTraceWidth`, and the unchanged 0.15mm default.

## How I tested

Ran locally with bun 1.3.14 (full suite is too heavy for my machine, so I ran the directories surrounding the change):

- `bun test tests/features/board-default-trace-width-autorouting.test.tsx tests/components/primitive-components/trace-default-trace-width.test.tsx tests/utils/autorouting/` — all pass (the new tests fail before the fix, reproducing the issue exactly: 0.15 instead of 0.3/0.25)
- `bun test tests/utils/ tests/components/primitive-components/ tests/components/normal-components/ tests/features/ tests/subcircuits/ tests/groups/ tests/drc/ tests/breakout/` — no new failures (`auto-jumper-autorouting`, `schematic-section-rp2040`, and `differential-pair/routing-phase` time out identically on unmodified `main` on my machine)

- `bun run format` — no changes

title: fix: <switch /> drops supplierPartNumbers/manufacturerPartNumber, part missing from BOM
description: Fixes issue where switch  component fails to propagate supplierPartNumbers and manufacturerPartNumber to the BOM, causing parts to be omitted without warning.
body:
Fixes tscircuit/tscircuit#4056

## Problem

`<switch />` accepts `supplierPartNumbers` (valid per `SwitchProps extends CommonComponentProps`), but `Switch.doInitialSourceRender()` builds the `source_component` with a fixed field list that omits `supplier_part_numbers` and `manufacturer_part_number`. The value silently disappears and the part never reaches the BOM — no type error, no warning.

Every other component type (`<chip />`, `<pushbutton />`, `<led />`, `<resistor />`, …) passes these through, e.g. PushButton:

```ts
supplier_part_numbers: props.supplierPartNumbers,
```

## Fix

Pass both fields through in `Switch.doInitialSourceRender()`, matching the pattern used by the other normal components (`manufacturerPartNumber ?? mfn` alias handling as in Resistor/Capacitor):

```ts
manufacturer_part_number: props.manufacturerPartNumber ?? props.mfn,
supplier_part_numbers: props.supplierPartNumbers,
```

## Test

Red→green test `tests/components/normal-components/switch-supplier-part-numbers.test.tsx`: renders a `<switch />` with `supplierPartNumbers={{ jlcpcb: ["C2681570"] }}` and `manufacturerPartNumber`, asserts both land on the `source_component`. Fails on main (`supplier_part_numbers` empty), passes with this change. Existing switch tests still pass; `tsc --noEmit` clean.

title: match unequal-side LGA footprints
description: Adds support for unequal-side LGA footprints by discovering perimeter LGA footprints with unequal pad counts, inferring pad dimensions, and generating explicit LGA grid candidates, while updating the JLC audit threshold from 98 to 95 IoU.
body:
## What changed

- discover perimeter LGA footprints with unequal pad counts on horizontal and vertical sides
- infer pad length and width from each pad's side orientation
- generate explicit `lgaN_gridAxB` candidates, including two-sided grids such as `grid3x0`
- preserve pill-pad geometry and prioritize the inferred explicit LGA grid
- update the JLC audit threshold from 98% to 95% IoU
- require `@tscircuit/footprinter@^0.0.385`, which contains the LGA generator from tscircuit/footprinter#722

## Why

The matcher previously assumed that four-sided packages had the same number of pads on every side and that the longer pad dimension always pointed inward. That prevented it from expressing common JLCPCB LGA layouts such as 5x3, 4x3, 4x2, 3x2, 2x4, and two-sided LGA-6 packages.

The 95% audit threshold keeps coverage work focused on materially missing footprint families rather than negligible edge-shape differences.

## Impact

On the full sequential 250-board `jlc5000` benchmark, this moves eight additional parts above 95% copper IoU:

- coverage increases from 171/250 (68.4%) to 179/250 (71.6%)
- seven new matches reach 100% IoU
- FSUSB42UMX-TP reaches 98.11% IoU
- benchmark errors remain at zero

## Validation

- `bun test` — 31 pass, 0 fail
- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun run format:check`
- `bun run build`
- full sequential 250-board benchmark against published `@tscircuit/footprinter@0.0.385`

- solver PR: https://github.com/tscircuit/power-trace-expander/pull/3
- step-through debugger: https://power-trace-expander.vercel.app

On the production fixture, the 1 mm routes improve as follows using Circuit JSON's length-weighted first-route-point segment-width semantics:

| Metric | Input | Expanded + cleaned |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| full-width coverage | 1.27% | 87.40% |
| coverage at or above 0.5 mm | 18.13% | 93.37% |
| average width | 0.232 mm | 0.938 mm |
| 5th percentile | 0.150 mm | 0.375 mm |

At the preferred 0.15 mm power-to-pad target, only 11 pad/trace pairs remain below target; every one still passes the hard 0.1 mm DRC.

title: Add half-width power pad clearance cleanup
description: Add bounded multilayer A rerouting for severe under-width intervals, including onetwo-via routes, endpoint necking, and transactional lower-priority trace shoves, along with debuggable post-route stages for redundant via-pair removal, power-to-pad clearance, and final path simplification.
body:
## Summary

- add bounded multilayer A* rerouting for severe under-width intervals, including one/two-via routes, endpoint necking, and transactional lower-priority trace shoves
- add debuggable post-route stages for redundant via-pair removal, power-to-pad clearance, and final 0/45/90-degree path simplification
- target unrelated-pad edge clearance at half of each power trace's nominal width by default, while accepting the best descending 0.025–0.05 mm tier when the full target cannot fit
- keep via-pair removal at the established 0.15 mm preferred-clearance tier, then let the dedicated clearance pass push the simpler route toward half width; this prevents clearance preservation from bringing redundant excursions back
- preserve the clearance achieved by the pad-spacing stage when the later simplifier rewrites a route
- keep prospective and existing routed vias out of connected pads, enforce drill spacing even on the same net, and relocate invalid vias without touching intentional footprint thermal vias
- retain the 10 mm local reroute bound and Flatbush-backed exact collision checks
- add `onlyConnectionNames` targeting through the solver and autorouter factory

## Debugger and integration

- deployed step-through debugger: https://power-trace-expander.vercel.app
- motor-controller integration: https://github.com/tscircuit/rp2040-motor-controller/pull/3

The debugger catalog has 13 simple and three complex fixtures. Focused cases cover full and constrained half-width clearance, routed-via-in-pad repair, clustered same-net via separation, direct and obstacle-aware via-pair elimination, and clearance shoving. Each scan, clearance tier, candidate, grid search, shove, rollback, and acceptance remains visible through the generic solver debugger.

The production regression now identifies the `R_ISEN_B` ground connection semantically and requires no via within 2 mm of either endpoint. The motor-controller integration separately verifies that the BISEN-side `R_ISEN_B` PCB trace is via-free.

## Measured result

For the captured board's 1 mm routes, Circuit JSON first-route-point width semantics improve from:

| Metric | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| full-width coverage | 1.27% | 87.39% |
| coverage at or above 0.5 mm | 18.13% | 93.57% |
| average width | 0.232 mm | 0.939 mm |
| 5th percentile | 0.150 mm | 0.375 mm |
| 10th percentile | 0.150 mm | 0.750 mm |
| normalized width deficit | 76.76% | 6.09% |

The stricter endpoint-minimum measurement reaches 86.19% full-width coverage, a 0.935 mm average, and a 6.53% normalized deficit. Cleanup removes seven redundant via pairs (14 vias), normalizes 63 arbitrary-angle segments, and commits five extra-clearance shoves.

The clearance histogram measures the same post-expansion geometry immediately before and after cleanup:

| Preferred pad clearance | Before cleanup | After cleanup |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 0.15 mm | 25 | 19 |
| 0.25 mm | 58 | 48 |
| 0.30 mm | 84 | 68 |
| 0.40 mm | 97 | 84 |
| 0.50 mm (half width) | 122 | 106 |

Removing the three additional redundant via pairs is a deliberate Pareto improvement over retaining their layer excursions: four more segment measurements remain below the aspirational 0.50 mm tier, while the direct routes remain DRC-clean and all six vias stay eliminated. Dense package escapes still satisfy the board's hard 0.1 mm rule. The via repair pass relocates five routed vias and leaves zero unresolved via violations.

Logic-route full-width coverage reaches 99.48%. A representative run completes in 15.6 seconds with 1.185M solver steps, 8,351 planar-grid attempts, and 51 layer-grid attempts, below the 20-second/4.1M-step regression gates.

The isolated upper `P_MOTOR_A` route retains its two-via lower-layer escape and greater than 97% conservative full-width coverage; its layer-change via remains outside the connected terminal pad.

## Validation

- `bun test` — 33 tests, 403 assertions
- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun run build`
- `bun run benchmark:rp2040`
- `git diff --check`
- solver SVG snapshots refreshed, including the full RP2040 Dual Motor fixture
- full `rp2040-motor-controller` render with `@tscircuit/checks`: no routing errors, no allowlist, no routed-via/pad overlaps, and no vias on the BISEN-side `R_ISEN_B` trace

## Summary

- add length-weighted trace-width measurement, a repeatable RP2040 benchmark, and residual bottleneck analysis
- widen clear geometry to the best safe intermediate width instead of only a few coarse candidates
- add a granular elastic solver that gently pushes lower-width blocking traces before falling back to obstacle-aware A*
- canonicalize connection aliases across source-trace names, merged names, PCB ports, traces, pads, and vias so same-net copper is not treated as an obstacle
- add exact capsule, polygon, and circle narrow-phase checks behind the Flatbush broad phase
- repeat productive board passes until copper-area gain falls below 0.1%, with a four-pass safety cap
- remove hot-path full-grid scans, reuse immutable spatial indices, and early-exit collision queries
- add an intermediate-width debugger fixture plus same-net, clearance, geometry, plateau, bottleneck, and performance regressions

## RP2040 Dual Motor result

Metrics use Circuit JSON's first-route-point segment-width semantics and are length weighted.

| 1 mm route metric | Input | Expanded |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| full-width coverage | 1.27% | 80.02% |
| coverage at or above 0.5 mm | 18.13% | 92.07% |
| average width | 0.232 mm | 0.906 mm |
| 5th percentile | 0.150 mm | 0.350 mm |
| 10th percentile | 0.150 mm | 0.500 mm |
| normalized width deficit | 76.76% | 9.41% |

The stricter endpoint-minimum lower bound reaches 78.06% full-width coverage and a 0.897 mm average. The 0.25 mm routes reach 99.47% full-width coverage. The 1 mm route length increases 5.73%.

The production fixture stops after three passes; the last adds only 0.013% of nominal copper area. A representative local run takes about 9.5–10.2 seconds versus about 23.8 seconds before these changes. The regression caps wall time, solver iterations, and attempted grids.

## DRC behavior

The motor-controller integration reruns `@tscircuit/checks` on the fully rendered board and reports no new routing DRCs beyond the same three pre-existing, explicitly allowlisted same-net ground-via spacing reports at the imported RP2040 boundary.

I also evaluated a more aggressive variant that let under-width power traces push peer power traces. It reached 82.77% full-width coverage, but the full-board DRC exposed different-net contacts, so that strategy is intentionally not included. Route-point transition checks remain conservative enough to match the integrated board DRC.

title: perf: share the base PrimitiveComponent config instead of rebuilding per access (#2810)
description: Reduces memory allocation by sharing the base PrimitiveComponent configuration instead of creating a new instance on each access.
body:
Progress on #2810 — the low-risk first slice of the suggested pure-TS fix.

## Change

The base `PrimitiveComponent.get config()` constructed a **fresh** `z.object({}).passthrough()` on every access:

```ts
get config(): BaseComponentConfig {
  return { componentName: "", zodProps: z.object({}).passthrough() }
}
```

`config` is a plain getter with no memo cache, accessed thousands of times per build, and each Zod v3 schema instance eagerly binds ~15 methods (`.parse`, `.safeParse`, `.refine`, …). The heap snapshot in tscircuit/tscircuit#4077 shows ~714k `native_bind` closures retained across ~47k schema instances, with the non-memoized base `get config()` called out as one of the two code-level causes.

The base config is now a module-level shared const — components that don't override `config` no longer allocate a schema (plus its ~15 bound closures) per access. Subclass configs already return module-level `zodProps` (`netProps`, `traceProps`, …) and are unchanged.

## Scope

This intentionally does **not** attempt the Zod v4 migration or a general per-class config memo (both larger, riskier follow-ups listed in the issue). It removes the one unambiguous per-access allocation.

## Verification

- Full `tests/components` suite: 562 pass, 1 fail — the failing `registers a differential pair using port selectors` test fails identically on `main` (pre-existing, unrelated)
- `bunx tsc --noEmit` / `biome check` — clean

title: Add standalone schematicsymbol element
description: Add a standalone schematicsymbol  backed by schematic-symbols, implementing it as a schematic-only PrimitiveComponent with support for explicit physical-port mapping and schematic sheetssections.
body:
## Summary

- add a standalone `<schematicsymbol />` backed by `schematic-symbols`
- implement it as a schematic-only `PrimitiveComponent`
- support explicit physical-port mapping when both `chipRef` and `connections` are provided
- support explicit schematic sheets/sections, placement, and rotation
- register the JSX intrinsic/export and bump `@tscircuit/props` to `^0.0.591`

## Connection API

`connections` maps labels exposed by `symbolName` (including `pinN` aliases) to explicit physical chip-port selectors:

```tsx
<schematicsymbol
  name="A"
  chipRef=".Q1"
  symbolName="n_channel_e_mosfet_transistor_horz"
  connections={{
    gate: "Q1.G1",
    source: "Q1.S1",
    drain: "Q1.D1",
  }}
/>

<trace from=".R1 > .pin2" to=".Q1 > .G1" />
```

The mapping does not create electrical traces. It projects the real chip ports into the symbol; normal `<trace>` elements continue to target the physical chip.

There is intentionally no automatic label matching. Supplying `chipRef` without `connections`, or `connections` without `chipRef`, emits a `source_property_ignored_warning` for the unmatched property and renders the symbol standalone. A symbol with neither remains a standalone schematic element.

## Architecture

- `SchematicSymbol` creates its own source component so the renderer displays `name` using the same `{REF}` mechanism as other components
- mapped schematic ports reuse the referenced physical chip's real `source_port_id` values
- qualified symbol names such as `_horz` and `_right` rotate through the shared `PrimitiveComponent` resolver, without a `SchematicSymbol` override
- connected components are not inferred onto a symbol's sheet; each visible component declares its own `schSheetName`
- no manual `schematic_text` insertion
- no shared `PrimitiveComponent`, `NormalComponent`, or `Port` lifecycle changes
- no PCB representation or missing-footprint behavior
- no `internalcircuit` dependency
- `displayName` rendering remains explicitly deferred until `schematic_component` has a `display_name` field

## Coverage

- standalone library symbol
- MOSFET and diode mappings with explicit connections
- two MOSFET representations (`A` and `B`) of one physical chip without a schematic sheet
- MOSFET and op-amp representations with separate traces across two explicitly assigned schematic sheets
- PCB snapshots confirming the referenced physical chips and their routed connections, without duplicate PCB components
- schematic-section participation
- warning-and-ignore behavior for incomplete `chipRef` + `connections` pairs, with no automatic port matching

## Validation

- 12 targeted schematic-symbol, symbol-rotation, and sheet regression tests pass
- `bun run build`
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- Biome checks for modified TypeScript files
- `git diff --check`
- full suite: 1,239 pass, 31 skip; one unrelated differential-pair PCB snapshot mismatch also reproduces in isolation

description: Fixes incorrect transform origin for nested groups in PCB layout, preventing footprint overlap errors in TI wireless subcircuits.

## Summary

- preserve the converter's initial aggregate component centers across the packing solver boundary
- use each aggregate center as the transform origin when applying packed nested-group positions
- update repro156 to assert that TI wireless subcircuits produce no footprint overlap errors
- refresh the PCB snapshot with the corrected placement

## Root cause

`convertCircuitJsonToPackOutput` expresses every descendant obstacle relative to a computed aggregate center. `convertPackOutputToPackInput` intentionally removes component centers before solving, and core then applied the packed group transform around `pcb_group.center`. For internally laid-out subcircuits that field can still be the default `(0, 0)`, so the solver's valid placement was translated from the wrong origin and the TI subcircuits overlapped.

The fix keeps the pre-solver pack output and uses its aggregate center when applying each nested-group transform, with `pcb_group.center` retained as a fallback.

title: Fix zero-height mobile containers preventing 3D preview and code editor rendering
description: Fixes zero-height mobile containers that prevent the 3D preview and code editor from rendering on mobile devices.
body:
Before: 

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/936e68fd-8390-4b37-a64a-10bb6602907c


After: 

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/63da030b-33dc-4447-b4de-fe65d012be13


### Motivation

The package editor’s 3D preview failed to render on mobile devices. When the responsive layout switched from a side-by-side row to a stacked column, the preview wrapper had no flexible height and collapsed to `0px`.

`SuspenseRunFrame` and its Three.js canvas depend on a non-zero parent height to calculate their rendering dimensions. As a result, the preview appeared completely blank even though the circuit loaded successfully.

The code editor was vulnerable to the same collapse when users switched to the Code view on mobile.

### Root cause

The mobile column layout relied on child containers expanding into the available vertical space, but the preview and code editor wrappers did not consistently use `flex-1`.

Their children used full-height layouts without receiving a defined height from their parents, causing the wrappers to collapse.

### User impact

Mobile users can now:

- Open a package and see its 3D preview.
- Switch between Preview and Code without either view collapsing.
- Continue using the existing desktop split layout without behavior changes.

### Reproduction

Before this fix:

1. Open a package editor on a mobile-width screen.
2. Switch to the 3D preview.
3. Observe that the preview area is blank because its wrapper has zero height.
4. Switch to the Code view and observe the same potential height collapse.

After this fix, both containers expand into the remaining vertical space and render normally.

title: Render multi-layer obstacles with red opacity
description: Render multi-layer obstacles in red with varying opacity based on the number of layers, while keeping bottom-only obstacles blue at 50 opacity.
body:
## Summary

- render each logical obstacle exactly once instead of once per z-layer
- keep bottom-only obstacles blue at 50% opacity
- render top-only and multi-layer obstacles red, with opacity increasing by canonical layer count: `1 - 0.5^N`
- preserve compound layer metadata such as `z0,1`

This is a separate implementation based directly on `main`. It replaces the neutral-gray multi-layer treatment from #1757 with the requested layer-weighted red opacity and does not alter #1737 or #1757.

## Why the color appeared to change

The obstacle's routing layers were not being mutated. The renderer emitted coincident rectangles for every z-layer, so semi-transparent colors accumulated at the same coordinates and the final visible color depended on layer/render order. This computes the equivalent red opacity on one rectangle instead.

Examples:
- 1 top layer: red at 50%
- 2 layers: red at 75%
- 3 layers: red at 87.5%

title: Avoid duplicate obstacles for packed nested groups
description: Fixes the issue of duplicate obstacles being emitted for nested groups in PCB packing by ensuring that components already represented by a top-level packed-group aggregate are not emitted again as fixed obstacles.
body:
## Summary

- make `convertCircuitJsonToPackOutput` track PCB components already represented by a top-level packed-group aggregate
- skip fixed-obstacle emission for relatively positioned descendants already contained by that aggregate
- preserve fixed obstacles for relatively positioned components directly under the packing root

## Why

A nested group is converted into one aggregate `PackedComponent`, but its relatively positioned member components were also emitted as fixed obstacles. The solver therefore saw the same physical geometry twice: once inside the movable group and once as immovable board geometry.

The deduplication belongs at the Circuit JSON → pack-output boundary, where both representations are created and their membership is known. This is the upstream fix needed by [tscircuit/core#2808](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/2808); core should not mutate `PackOutput` after conversion.

## What changed

- Normalize `um` and `µm` length values to millimeters before footprint-specific parsers run.
- Apply normalization to both footprinter strings and the fluent builder API.
- Support compound dimensions such as `thermalpad2400umx3000um`.
- Add SVG snapshot coverage for simple and compound micrometer dimensions.

## Why

Micrometer support was inconsistent across footprint families. Families using the shared `circuit-json` length schema already parsed `um`, while families using `parseFloat` or `@tscircuit/mm` treated `100um` as `100mm` or rejected it. This prevented `circuit-json-to-footprinter` from safely emitting shorter sub-millimeter values.

After this change, micrometer values are equivalent to their millimeter forms across all footprint families and numeric parameters.

## Validation

title: Fix duplicate orientation canvas in StrictMode
description: Fixes a bug where a duplicate orientation canvas is created in StrictMode due to improper cleanup of effect-owned resources.
body:
## Summary

- clean up each orientation-cube effect using the exact canvas and animation frame created by that effect instance
- stop resolving effect-owned resources through mutable React refs during cleanup
- add a Strict Mode regression test that fails with two canvases before the fix and passes with one after it

## Root cause

`OrientationCubeCanvas` appends its canvas imperatively in a passive effect. During React 19 Strict Mode's effect replay, React clears the DOM ref before running the passive-effect cleanup. The cleanup guarded removal with `containerRef.current`, which was therefore `null`, so the old canvas stayed attached. When setup replayed, it appended a second canvas to the same 120×120 container. Normal document flow pushed the real orientation cube down by 120px while the orphan appeared as the broken-looking box in Runframe.

The cleanup now closes over the exact canvas, renderer, scene, camera, and animation frame created by the effect. `canvas.remove()` no longer depends on ref timing and runs before Three.js resource disposal.

title: Use schematic port IDs in the schematic trace solver
description: Fixes net-label routing when a chip and schematicbox chipRef... render the same source pin by using canonical schematic_port_id values as schematic trace-solver pin IDs end to end.
body:
## Summary

- use canonical `schematic_port_id` values as schematic trace-solver pin IDs end to end
- remove `getSchematicPortSelector` and the selector-to-port translation maps
- fix net-label routing when a `<chip>` and `<schematicbox chipRef="...">` render the same source pin
- strengthen the repro156 regression test and refresh the affected schematic snapshots

## Root cause

The trace solver used CSS-like selectors such as `U1.8` as its internal pin identity. That works while one source pin has one schematic representation.

In repro156, the chip and its schematic box both render the same source pin. Both ports therefore produced the same selector. Because the routing code stored ports in maps keyed by that selector, one rendered port overwrote the other and the net label could be routed to the wrong representation.

Each rendered schematic port already has a unique canonical `schematic_port_id`, so creating another identity from the component name and pin number was unnecessary.

## Fix

The solver now receives `schematic_port_id` directly and its output is consumed as schematic port IDs. There is no component-name suffix, port-ID suffix, or fallback selector.

The existing internally-connected-pin dedup behavior is preserved: its representative port ID is used only to detect duplicates, while the original schematic port ID is passed to the solver. The adjacent port lookup is keyed by `schematic_port_id` so separate schematic representations of one source port do not overwrite each other.

Removing `getSchematicPortSelector` only removes this internal routing identity layer. User-facing selectors such as `U1.GND` and `.pin1` still work normally; the public selector system is unchanged.

## Snapshot impact

The minimum-spanning-tree routing solver uses pin IDs to break equal-cost ties. Replacing derived selector strings with canonical port IDs can therefore select a different, but electrically equivalent, route in tied layouts. The affected schematic snapshots are refreshed accordingly.

The pushbutton internally-connected-pin snapshot is unchanged.

## Validation

- repro156 regression test passes
- `pushbutton-pin-configurations` and repro155 internally-connected-pin tests pass
- relevant schematic trace and section tests pass
- TypeScript typecheck passes
- package build passes

title: fix: propagate manufacturerPartNumber and supplierPartNumbers in transistor, crystal, fuse, potentiometer, and interconnect
description: Fixes the issue where manufacturerPartNumber and supplierPartNumbers were not being propagated to the source_component for several components, causing them to be omitted from the BOM.
body:
Fixes #2787

## Problem

`<transistor />`, `<crystal />`, `<fuse />`, `<potentiometer />`, and `<interconnect />` accept `supplierPartNumbers` and `manufacturerPartNumber` (valid per their props, which extend `CommonComponentProps`), but each component's `doInitialSourceRender()` builds the `source_component` with a fixed field list that omits `supplier_part_numbers` and `manufacturer_part_number`. The values silently disappear and the parts never reach the BOM — no type error, no warning.

Same defect as the `<switch />` fix (tscircuit#4056 → #2765) and the `<mosfet />` fix (#2776 → #2778). Found by auditing every `db.source_component.insert` call site in `lib/` for the missing fields after those merges; these five are the remaining affected components (`EnclosureFdmBox` also omits the fields but its props reject them, so it is excluded).

## Fix

Pass both fields through in each `doInitialSourceRender()`, matching the pattern used by the other normal components (`manufacturerPartNumber ?? mfn` alias handling as in Resistor/Switch/Mosfet):

```ts
manufacturer_part_number: props.manufacturerPartNumber ?? props.mfn,
supplier_part_numbers: props.supplierPartNumbers,
```

Two lines per component; Interconnect additionally gets the same `const { _parsedProps: props } = this` destructure the others already use.

## Test

Red→green tests in `tests/components/normal-components/supplier-part-numbers-propagation.test.tsx` — one per component, each rendering the component with a real JLCPCB part (MMBT3904/C20526, X322516MLB4SI/C13738, SMD1206P050TF/C20799, 3296W-1-103LF/C34846, 0603WAF0000T5E/C21189) and asserting both fields land on the `source_component`. All five fail on main (`undefined`), all pass with this change. Full `bun test` suite, `tsc --noEmit`, and `biome format` clean.

title: fix: align transistor pin aliases/accessors with schematic-symbols (pin1=collector, pin2=base, pin3=emitter)
description: Fixes incorrect transistor pin aliases and accessors to align with schematic symbols, resolving issues in SPICE netlist generation.
body:
Fixes tscircuit/tscircuit#3617

## Root cause

The `schematic-symbols` package numbers the BJT ports as **pin1 = collector, pin2 = base, pin3 = emitter** — identically for `npn_bipolar_transistor` and `pnp_bipolar_transistor`, in both `_horz` and `_vert` orientations (verified against the currently-pinned `schematic-symbols@0.0.232`):

```
npn_bipolar_transistor_horz / pnp_bipolar_transistor_horz:
  ["1","collector"]  x=-0.55  y= 0.29
  ["2","base"]       x= 0.00  y=-0.40
  ["3","emitter"]    x= 0.55  y= 0.29
```

`Transistor.ts` disagreed with this in two places at once:

```ts
// aliases said pin2=emitter, pin3=base (symbol says pin2=base, pin3=emitter)
pin1: ["collector", "c"], pin2: ["emitter", "e"], pin3: ["base", "b"]

// and the accessors even disagreed with the aliases directly above them
emitter = this.portMap.pin1   // pin1 is aliased "collector"!
collector = this.portMap.pin2
base = this.portMap.pin3
```

Because schematic positions are assigned by pin number, ports ended up with **contradictory port_hints** — e.g. pin2 carried both `"base"` (from the symbol) and `"emitter"` (from the alias) — so name-based selectors and downstream consumers resolved pins arbitrarily.

## This was corrupting SPICE netlists, not just symbol positions

`circuit-json-to-spice` resolves BJT terminals by port hints. With the contradictory hints, the switch-circuit test (`ngspice-spice-analysis01-switch`) generated:

```
before:  SSW1 N2 0 ...      ← switch output shorted to ground
         QQ1  N3 0 0 NPN    ← base AND emitter both on node 0 (B-E short, transistor can never turn on)
after:   SSW1 N2 N3 ...
         QQ1  N4 N3 0 NPN   ← collector=N4, base=N3, emitter=GND — correct
```

The old simulation snapshot showed a flat collector voltage (transistor permanently off); the updated snapshot shows the correct 0↔5 V switching waveform. That's why the two snapshot updates in this PR are part of the fix, not incidental churn.

## Answers to the questions raised on the earlier attempts (props#698, props#714, core#2541 — all stale-closed)

- **@imrishabh18 "Wouldn't this mess up the PNP mapping?"** — No: the PNP symbol uses the *same* numbering as NPN (`pin1=collector, pin2=base, pin3=emitter`, verified above), so one mapping fixes both. The new test asserts positions for **both** npn and pnp.
- **@ShiboSoftwareDev "is this consistent within the repo?"** — Both BJT symbol variants and both orientations agree. MOSFET/JFET symbols use their own gate/source/drain labels and are untouched by this change (the `Mosfet` component has its own mapping; `mosfet-symbol-port-sides.test.tsx` still passes).
- Note the earlier core attempt (#2541) proposed `pin2=emitter`, which contradicts the symbols package — merging it would have swapped base and emitter.

## Changes

- `Transistor.ts`: aliases → `pin1: ["collector","c"], pin2: ["base","b"], pin3: ["emitter","e"]`; accessors → `collector=pin1, base=pin2, emitter=pin3`.
- `transistor-ports.test.tsx`: two new tests — (1) the schematic port named collector/base/emitter must sit at the symbol port with that label, for npn **and** pnp (red on `main`: 2 fail → green here); (2) accessors must match the aliases.
- Regenerated the two affected snapshots (schematic layout + the now-physically-correct ngspice switch simulation).

Ran `tsc --noEmit` (clean), `biome check` (clean), and every test file referencing transistors (12 pass / 0 fail), plus the spice-analysis suite.

A follow-up PR to `props` aligning `transistorPins` (`pin1=emitter, pin2=collector` there today) with the same order is ready; it's independent of this fix.

---

title: Reuse schematic symbol ports for trace routing
description: Refactors schematic routing to reuse existing schematic symbol ports for trace routing, improving efficiency and clarity in the routing process.

## Summary

This is a cleaner alternative to #2775 and #2768.

- add one helper that returns the physical port supplying a pin's existing schematic symbol port
- keep the first physical pin for each shared schematic symbol port when building one named-net solver input
- mark all physical pins using a routed schematic symbol port as connected
- preserve all physical `schematic_port` and `source_trace` records
- use distinct branded `SchematicPortId` and `SourcePortId` types throughout schematic routing
- avoid coordinate matching
- add regression assertions for both visible labels, exact GND trace termination, and connected physical GND pins

## Why this is cleaner

The component has already assigned `schematicSymbolPortDef` before schematic routing starts. The routing code can use that assignment directly.

Unlike #2775, this version does not build a port-ID map in the solver input and pass it through the schematic render orchestration to the output step. Both routing stages call the same small helper instead.

Pins using different schematic symbol ports remain separate, even when electrically internally connected. Explicitly positioned ports and imported Circuit JSON ports also remain separate.

The branded IDs prevent source-port and schematic-port identifiers from being mixed inside routing sets and maps. The conversion from Circuit JSON's current string fields happens only at the routing boundary.

title: Scope weighted connection filtering to participating pads
description: Scope weighted connection filtering to pads that actually participate in weighted metadata, ensuring that only explicitly listed pad pairs are eligible for placement scoring while preserving normal same-network fallback for unrelated unweighted pads.
body:
## Summary

- scope weighted-connection filtering to pads that actually participate in weighted metadata
- keep explicitly listed pad pairs eligible for placement scoring
- preserve normal same-network fallback for unrelated unweighted pads
- continue rejecting unlisted alternatives for pads whose weighted connection sets `ignoreWeakConnections: true`
- update the three visual snapshots whose ordinary same-net passives now influence placement

## Why

Previously, adding any `weightedConnections` entry changed the list into a global allowlist. A direct connection hint for one pair therefore made every unlisted pair in the entire pack input weak, including unrelated chip-to-passive connections. That removed most passive proximity targets and contributed to linear-looking packing.

This change does **not** make every electrical connection strong. Callers first require matching `networkId`, then this helper applies the following policy:

| Pair | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Explicitly listed together | considered |
| Neither pad appears in weighted metadata | considered through the normal same-network fallback |
| Either pad participates in an `ignoreWeakConnections: true` entry, but the pair is unlisted | ignored |
| Participating entry allows weak connections | considered through the same-network fallback |

The numeric `weight` field is unchanged; this PR only fixes which same-network targets are eligible.

## Validation

- `bun test` — 120 pass, 10 skip, 0 fail
- `bun run typecheck`
- `bunx biome check lib/utils/isStrongConnection.ts tests/is-strong-connection.test.ts`

title: Support schematic port IDs in net label grouping
description: Fixes net label grouping by resolving opaque pin IDs to their owning chips, ensuring uniform GND rail behavior in schematic outputs.
body:
## Summary

- resolve opaque pin IDs such as `schematic_port_29` to their owning chip through `InputProblem.chips`
- retain historical merged-group IDs for legacy component-qualified pins such as `J2.13`
- add a focused unit test for schematic-port grouping
- add the exact current `@tscircuit/core` RP2040 gamepad solver input and a visual regression proving uniform GND rails

## Root cause

`groupLabelsByChipAndOrientation` inferred component ownership with `pinId.split(".")[0]`. That worked for legacy IDs such as `J2.13`, but Core now passes schematic port IDs such as `schematic_port_29`, which contain no component prefix. Every port was therefore treated as a separate component during netlabel merging.

Because adjacent labels were not merged into component-side obstacles, the trace/label overlap stage rerouted individual GND branches around separate labels. Those detours produced the staggered rails seen in Core even with schematic-trace-solver 0.0.109.

The fix uses the chip/pin relationship already present in the solver input as the source of truth for opaque IDs. The prior cleanup-stage workaround has been removed from the final diff.

## Impact

Current Core output with schematic-port IDs now follows the same component-side label grouping behavior as legacy component-qualified pin IDs. The RP2040 repro produces one uniform GND rail on each side of the chip without weakening rail-alignment readability checks.

## Validation

- `bun test` — 146 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failed
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`

title: Emit compact 10 µm footprint dimensions
description: Rounds generated footprint dimensions to the nearest 10 m and emits positive dimensions below 0.1 mm as integer um values, while keeping larger dimensions in mm form.
body:
## What changed

- Round generated footprint dimensions to the nearest 10 µm (0.01 mm).
- Emit positive dimensions below 0.1 mm as integer `um` values.
- Keep dimensions at or above 0.1 mm in concise `mm` form.
- Apply the same quantization to optimized parameters, generated seeds, and compound thermal-pad dimensions.

For example, `0.05mm` becomes `50um`, while `0.1mm`, `0.55mm`, and larger dimensions remain in millimeters.

## Why

The formatter previously emitted up to four decimal places followed by `mm`, producing unnecessarily long strings and precision below what footprint matching needs. Integer micrometer values are shorter for very small dimensions, and 10 µm resolution keeps the geometry within the intended tolerance without making common sub-millimeter values less readable.

## Dependency

This PR depends on [tscircuit/footprinter#729](https://github.com/tscircuit/footprinter/pull/729), which makes `um` parsing consistent across all footprint families, fluent-builder parameters, and compound dimensions. The formatter suite passes with its current declared dependency; full cross-family compatibility was additionally validated against the linked footprinter branch. The dependency should be bumped to the released footprinter version before this PR merges.
